cell_edits.Est. cost & time: Association registration ISK 30,000 (Skatturinn); 2-4 weeks. Non-business foundations need a minimum endowment of ISK 1,750,000 (2026) plus an ISK 14,000 charter-confirmation fee; foreigners may found.
cell_edits.Key local requirements: Icelandic registered address and local contact; association needs ~5 members; foundation needs ISK 1.75m minimum endowment (2026) and charter confirmation by the Westfjords District Commissioner

finding: Skatturinn's fee schedule lists ISK 30,000 to register an association or public-benefit association (félagasamtök / almannaheillafélag), not ISK 5,000-10,000. Island.is states the 2026 minimum endowment for a foundation under a confirmed charter is ISK 1,750,000, with an ISK 14,000 confirmation fee, and that the Westfjords District Commissioner confirms charters; the old ISK 1m and ISK 3m figures were inconsistent and outdated, and no board-residency rule is stated.

cell_edits.Est. cost & time: PRH association fee EUR 60 (guided online) or EUR 120 (other filings); 1-3 months. Foreigners may be members; no residency requirement to found an association.

finding: PRH's current price list charges EUR 60 for an association start-up notification filed through the guided online process and EUR 120 for other electronic or paper filings, not a flat ~EUR 100. PRH describes the guided online route as the fastest and cheapest; the other claims (Associations Act 503/1989, Foundations Act 487/2015) were not contradicted.

Registering an ekonomisk förening with Bolagsverket costs SEK 1,900 through the verksamt.se e-service (SEK 2,200 on paper) in 2026, matching the cell. Ideell förening organisation numbers come from Skatteverket, and foundations register with the county administrative board (länsstyrelsen), as stated.

cell_edits.Registration fee (USD): $0 (CVR registration of a voluntary association is free)

finding: Erhvervsstyrelsen guidance says registering a voluntary association (frivillig forening) for a CVR number via Virk is free, renewed every 3 years, and requires MitID, so the ~$20 fee was wrong. LBK nr. 2020 of 11/12/2020 is confirmed as the current consolidated Act on Foundations and Certain Associations (amended through Act 1703/2024).

cell_edits.Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Latvian address and Latvian-language documents; without a Latvian/EU e-signature, notarised signatures are needed, so a local representative is practical (no board residency rule)

finding: Cabinet Regulation No. 308 (2004, in force) sets a EUR 11.38 state fee to register an association or foundation, with 90% payable when filed via the Enterprise Register online form, confirming the fee cells. The Associations and Foundations Law requires at least two founders and sets only age/legal-capacity conditions for board members (s. 42(3)), with no Latvian residence requirement, so the 'Latvian-resident board' bottleneck was removed.

Lei 24/2012 (Lei-Quadro das Fundações) remains in force as amended by Leis 150/2015, 36/2021 and 67/2021; recognition of private foundations rests with the Prime Minister (delegable) and can be refused for insufficient assets. A 2025 working group (Despacho 2820/2025) is reviewing the framework, but no replacement law was found; official recognition fees and decision times were not published in the sources checked.

Vatican City State has no public charity or company registry open to private filers; legal persons there are erected or recognised by Holy See/State authorities under the Fundamental Law and canon law. No fee or standard timeline exists, so the existing 'no' foreign-founder answer and case-by-case description stand.

Circular 10/AM/2006 confirms associations are formed by notification to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities, which issues a receipt (ilm wa khabar) after reviewing bylaws, founder names and judicial records, and refers the association for publication in the Official Gazette. The circular sets no fee or deadline and contains no foreigner-specific provisions, consistent with the existing cells.

A September 2026 position paper says the Ministry of Social Affairs and Labor has only completed an initial draft of a law to replace Law 93 of 1958, which has not yet gone to the People's Assembly. A February 2026 association licence was issued under Law 93/1958 and its bylaws (Decree 1330), confirming Law 93 still governs.

cell_edits.Est. cost & time: No statutory fee (Law 12/2010 Art. 7 exempts applications from duties), but founders must be Iraqi nationals or Iraq residents, so non-resident foreigners cannot found directly. Statutory: 7-day decision on establishment, certificate within 30 days of a complete application.
cell_edits.Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Founders (min. 3) must be Iraqi nationals or Iraq residents; local address, Arabic filings with the Council of Ministers NGO Department

finding: Law 12 of 2010 requires an application signed by at least three founders who are Iraqi nationals or residents (Arts. 4-5), filed with the NGOs Department of the Council of Ministers Secretariat (Art. 1). Article 7 exempts establishment and registration applications from duties, and Article 8 sets a 7-day establishment decision (deemed approval) and a 30-day certificate deadline, contradicting the '$200-1,000' fee, 'times unpublished' and '10 Iraqi founders / MoSAL' claims.

cell_edits.Key local requirements: Moroccan registered office, Arabic statutes; declaration filed with the local administrative authority (caïdat/pashalik), which issues a receipt; declaratory regime, not approval; foreign founders permitted.
cell_edits.Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Registered office + Arabic statutes; local authorities can delay or withhold the declaration receipt; local address agent usually needed

finding: Under Dahir 1-58-376 of 1958 as amended by Law 75-00, an association is formed by a declaration filed at the local administrative authority for its seat, which issues a stamped provisional receipt; no prior authorisation or governor approval is required. The practical obstacle documented by HRW is authorities refusing or delaying the receipt, so 'governor approval/discretion' was replaced.

cell_edits.Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Local CSOs may be founded only by Ethiopians and/or Ethiopia-resident foreigners; a non-resident founder must use a partner or register a foreign CSO with ACSO, which needs local representation.

finding: CSO Proclamation No. 1113/2019 defines a local organisation as one formed by Ethiopians, foreigners resident in Ethiopia, or both, and registration is with the Authority for Civil Society Organizations (ACSO), so the bottleneck's 'Ethiopian-national founders' and 'CSO Agency' wording was wrong. The restrictive 2025 amendment drafted by the Ministry of Justice and ACSO had not been put to parliament as of HRW and Amnesty reporting in mid-2025, and no enactment was found.
